name: Milwaukee
meta_description: TDSC investigative consulting in matters touching Milwaukee: manufacturing acquisitions, trade secret disputes, fintech and healthcare fraud, litigation.
hero_lede: Milwaukee is Wisconsin's largest city and a centre for advanced manufacturing, financial services, insurance and healthcare. TDSC scopes investigative consulting from Nashville for matters touching the city, coordinating Wisconsin counsel and Wisconsin-licensed private detectives where work in the state requires a licence.
intro: Milwaukee is Wisconsin's largest city, with 563,305 residents in the Census Bureau's July 2022 estimate and about 2 million people across the seven-county region. It is home to the headquarters of Fortune 500 companies including Northwestern Mutual, ManpowerGroup, Fiserv, WEC Energy Group and Rockwell Automation, with Kohl's in the metropolitan area, and to Fortune 1000 manufacturers such as Harley-Davidson, A.O. Smith and Generac nearby. Health systems, led by Advocate Aurora, Froedtert and Ascension, are the largest employers. Manufacturing employs over 115,000 people in the region, including GE Healthcare, Milwaukee Tool and Johnson Controls operations, alongside a significant financial services and professional services base.

Organisations commission investigative work connected to Milwaukee because of its concentration of industrial know-how, family and founder-owned manufacturers, and large financial and healthcare institutions. Private equity firms and strategic buyers acquiring regional manufacturers need to test management, related-party dealings and litigation history. Manufacturers face departing-employee and trade secret disputes involving competitors. Insurers, payment companies and health systems deal with fraud schemes, vendor misconduct and internal investigations. Litigation in the Milwaukee County Circuit Court and the federal court in Milwaukee generates demand for witness location, background research and asset tracing to support judgment enforcement.

matters.title: Manufacturing acquisition due diligence
matters.text: Buyers of founder and family-owned manufacturers around Milwaukee need assurance on owners, managers and the business. We research principals' backgrounds, related-party entities, litigation, liens, regulatory history and media, and test management representations, giving deal teams findings they can raise before signing.

matters.title: Trade secret and departing employee matters
matters.text: Milwaukee's engineering and automation firms compete for talent and know-how. When key staff leave for competitors or start rival businesses, we research new ventures, corporate filings, public statements and relationships, supporting counsel in assessing restrictive covenant and trade secret claims through lawful sources.

matters.title: Insurance and financial services fraud
matters.text: Insurers, payment processors and wealth managers headquartered in the region face claims fraud, merchant fraud and misconduct by agents or intermediaries. We support internal and counsel-directed investigations with background research, corporate mapping, asset research and, through licensed Wisconsin detectives, lawful field inquiries.

matters.title: Healthcare vendor and billing integrity
matters.text: Large health systems rely on many suppliers, staffing firms and billing contractors. We research vendors' ownership, conflicts of interest with employees, exclusion and enforcement history and litigation, supporting compliance teams and counsel investigating suspected kickbacks, billing irregularities or procurement misconduct.

matters.title: Litigation support and judgment recovery
matters.text: Parties in Milwaukee commercial litigation need witnesses located, counterparties profiled and assets identified. We research public court, property and corporate records in Wisconsin and other states, giving counsel factual material for case strategy, settlement and enforcement of judgments.

local_context.title: Milwaukee County Circuit Court
local_context.text: The Milwaukee County Circuit Court has 47 branches, the most of any Wisconsin circuit court, and hears civil, criminal, family and probate matters for the county. Its chief judge serves full-time in an administrative role. Wisconsin circuit court case information is generally searchable online, making local litigation history an accessible research source when profiling Milwaukee individuals and businesses. Appeals go to the Wisconsin Court of Appeals.

local_context.title: Wisconsin commercial docket
local_context.text: Wisconsin has no permanent dedicated business court in Milwaukee. In 2017 the Wisconsin Supreme Court created a commercial docket pilot based in Waukesha County, later extended statewide in 2019 and to Dane County in 2020. On 7 October 2024 the court voted 4 to 3 to stop assigning new cases to the pilot, so complex commercial cases are now heard on general dockets.

local_context.title: Private detective licensing
local_context.text: Wisconsin requires both private detective agencies and individual detectives to be licensed by the Department of Safety and Professional Services (DSPS). Individuals must work under a licensed agency, pass a state exam and a fingerprint-based background check, and carry liability coverage. Acting as a private detective without a licence violates Wis. Stat. 440.26(8). Fieldwork in Milwaukee is therefore done by Wisconsin-licensed detectives.

local_context.title: Federal court and state registries
local_context.text: Federal cases arising in Milwaukee, including securities, fraud and intellectual property disputes, are heard in the US District Court for the Eastern District of Wisconsin, which sits in the city. Wisconsin business entities file with the Department of Financial Institutions, and real property records are kept by the Milwaukee County Register of Deeds. Both are standard sources for ownership and asset research.

tdsc_approach: TDSC has no office in Milwaukee and works on Milwaukee matters from Nashville. We agree the purpose with the client and its counsel first, whether acquisition diligence on a manufacturer, a departing employee or trade secret concern, a fraud inquiry or litigation support, and scope research to it. Sources include Wisconsin circuit court and federal court records, state business entity filings, county property records, regulatory actions and media. Because Wisconsin licenses private detectives through DSPS, any surveillance, interviews or other fieldwork in Milwaukee is carried out by Wisconsin-licensed detectives. We do not use pretexting or access restricted records, and personal data is handled under applicable federal and state law.

faqs.q: Does TDSC work in Milwaukee with a Wisconsin licence?
faqs.a: TDSC works from Nashville and has no Milwaukee office. Wisconsin requires private detectives and agencies to be licensed by the Department of Safety and Professional Services, so any fieldwork, such as surveillance or in-person inquiries, is carried out by Wisconsin-licensed detectives that we coordinate. Desk-based research uses public records and lawful sources.

faqs.q: Is there a business court in Milwaukee?
faqs.a: Not a permanent one. Wisconsin's commercial docket pilot, created in 2017 and based in Waukesha County, was extended statewide in 2019, but the Wisconsin Supreme Court stopped assigning new cases to it in October 2024. Commercial cases are heard in the Milwaukee County Circuit Court or, for federal matters, the Eastern District of Wisconsin.

faqs.q: Can you help investigate a departing employee who joined a competitor?
faqs.a: Yes, through lawful means. We research the competitor and any new venture, corporate filings, public profiles, statements and relationships, and coordinate licensed Wisconsin detectives where fieldwork is needed. Forensic review of company devices and accounts is done by digital forensics specialists, and legal claims and covenants are matters for the client's counsel.

faqs.q: What can you find on a Milwaukee manufacturer before an acquisition?
faqs.a: We review the company and its principals through state entity filings, circuit and federal court records, liens, property records, regulatory and environmental actions, and media. We look for related-party businesses, prior failures, disputes with customers or employees and inconsistencies with what management has told the buyer, and report each finding with its source.

faqs.q: Can you trace assets to enforce a judgment in Wisconsin?
faqs.a: We research public property, corporate, lien, court and other records in Wisconsin and other states to identify assets and related entities connected to a judgment debtor. We do not obtain bank records or other restricted data without lawful process. Garnishment, discovery and other enforcement steps are pursued by counsel through the courts.
